tur59-1: Pain changes during the day and from day to day, while the pain we remember afterwards can be strongly coloured by the most intense moments and the most recent ones. Your entries give you a more balanced picture.
tur59-2: See a doctor if your pain is new, getting steadily worse, or comes with other symptoms. In the guides in the Health library you can find, for each condition, when to seek help without delay. In long-lasting pain, a “boom and bust” cycle is common: you do too much on a good day, the pain flares, and then you move less for a while. One NHS leaflet suggests finding a starting level for important activities that you can manage without increasing your pain, and building it up very gradually; your diary can help you spot this cycle.

tur59-9: People usually walk further on their second attempt: in people with COPD the second test is on average 26 metres longer. So if you are doing it for the first time, you can repeat the test once fully rested and record the better result.
